Alex / Neha —

Quick summary from the runtime side after an initial triage:
- Root cause: the safety valve attached to HarborEdge's quota profile (profile id: prof-HS12145) entered a hard-close state during the ramp. The valve's burst_window and token_bucket were set conservatively (burst_size=250 tokens) and the recent traffic pattern with short high-frequency bursts exhausted the bucket and immediately dropped to hard deny for new requests.
- Behavior observed: when the safety valve moved to hard-close it triggered request rejection (429/503 depending on route) and caused head-of-line latency increases as clients retried. The rate limiter logs show repeated drop events from 07:42:09 — 07:57:00 PDT.

Immediate mitigation we've prepared:
1) Temporarily increase burst_size to 1,000 tokens for HS-12145 (will reduce early rejections).
2) Relax safety_valve hysteresis so it doesn't hard-close on short bursts (temporary change).
3) Disable the aggressive per-customer emergency throttle for 20 minutes to let traffic settle; monitor 95/99 latencies.

We can enact 1+2 now with operator approval. Rollback plan: revert the changes at 09:30 PDT or sooner if downstream capacity issues arise. I'll also enable a short-lived traffic shadow to check for latent overload.

Logs and the specific sequences are attached to the incident ticket (internal).

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
